question:
Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

If I had found (A)/ her phone number, (B)/ I have called her. (C)/ No error (D)
solution:
The erroneous part is option 3) i.e. 'I have called her'.

Key Points

  •  In the given sentence the error lies in the part 'I have called her'.
  • The sentence is a conditional sentence & its structure is:
    • ​If+ past perfect+ sub+ would+ have+ V3+ object​
  • ​Example:
    • ​If she had got the recipe for shrimp, she would have cooked it.
  • ​Therefore, we have to add 'would' before 'have' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct sentence: If I had found her phone number, I would have called her.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The sports day events / will be conducted / from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. / on Saturday.
solution:
The correct answer is 'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.' should be used instead of 'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.'.
  • We know that the preposition 'from' is followed by 'to'.
  • We use 'from … to' to talk about ranges of different things
    • Example: Sir Edward Youde was the Governor of Hong Kong from 1982 to 1985.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct Sentence: The sports day events will be conducted from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturday

question:
Choose the option that is the passive form of the given sentence.

Did they tell you to attend the meeting?
options: Have you told to attend the meeting?
You were expected to attend the meeting.
Were you told to attend the meeting?
Have you been told to attend the meeting?
solution:
The passive form of the sentence is 'Were you told to attend the meeting?'.

Key Points

Simple Past Tense:

The simple past tense is used to talk about a completed action in a time before now. 

  • The instructions given below should be followed while changing an Interrogative Sentence​ to a passive voice.
    • Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases as well if subject and object are pronouns.
    • If any Interrogative Sentence starts from 'do, does or did' then while preparing Passive Voice, the candidates should use 'is/are/am/was and were' according to the Number & Person of Object.
    • Use appropriate helping verb as per tense. (simple past - was/were).
    • Always use the third form of the main verb. (told)
    • At last line up the remaining part.
       

So, the final sentence is - Were you told to attend the meeting?

Hinglish
सरल भूतकाल:

सिंपल पास्ट टेंस का इस्तेमाल अब से पहले के समय में पूरी हुई क्रिया के बारे में बात करने के लिए किया जाता है।

  • Interrogative sentence को passive voice में बदलते समय नीचे दिए गए निर्देशों का पालन किया जाना चाहिए।
    • वाक्य के subject और object का पता लगाएं और उनके स्थानों को exchange करें; उनके cases में भी परिवर्तन करें यदि subject और object pronouns हैं।
    • यदि कोई interrogative sentence 'do, does or did' से प्रारंभ होता है तो passive voice तैयार करते समय candidates को वस्तु की संख्या और व्यक्ति के अनुसार 'is/are/am/was and were' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
    • Tense के अनुसार helping verb का प्रयोग करें। (simple past - was/were)
    • हमेशा main verb के third form का प्रयोग करें। (told)

question:
Direction: Choose the option that best transforms the sentence into its Direct / Indirect form:

‘Beware of pickpockets,’ said a huge notice.
options: A huge notice has claimed us to beware of pickpockets.
A huge notice instructed us to be aware of pickpockets.
A huge notice warned us to beware of pickpockets.
A huge notice is warning all the public to beware.
solution:
The correct answer is '​A huge notice warned us to beware of pickpockets.'

Key Points 

  • The reporting verb 'said/said to' is changed in 'asked, demanded, ordered, enquired, offered' as per the nature of the sentence.
  • The first person in reported speech changes according to the subject of reporting speech.
  • In Reported Speech change of the second person depends on the object of reporting speech.
  • The third person remains unchanged.
  • Imperative sentences do not normally have an expressed subject.
  • This is because the subject ‘you’ is usually understood.
  • As a result of this, imperative sentences begin with a verb in the simple present tense.
  • In order to change an imperative sentence into indirect speech, we use a to-infinitive.
  • Example: 
    • The old woman said to the boy, ‘Please help me.’
    • The old woman requested the boy to help her.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct sentence: A huge notice warned us to beware of pickpockets.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Break a leg
solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Break a leg" means to wish someone good luck, especially in a performance or presentation. (शुभकामनाएं देना)
    • Example: Before the play, all the actors told each other to break a leg.
  • "Wish good luck" means to express hope that someone will succeed. (शुभकामनाएं देना)
    • Example: She wished her friend good luck before the big exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Wish good luck.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Hurt yourself (खुद को चोट पहुँचाना): To cause physical harm to oneself.
    • Example: Be careful with that knife, you might hurt yourself.
  • Wish bad luck (बुरी किस्मत की कामना करना): To hope that something bad happens to someone.
    • Example: It’s not good to wish bad luck on others.
  • Sprain a leg (पैर में मोच आना): To injure a leg by twisting it suddenly.
    • Example: He sprained his leg while playing football.

question:
In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Let I do (A)/this work for (B)/my bright future. (C)/No error (D)
solution:
The correct answer is ‘Part A’.
Key Points
  • The above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • The error lies in part A of the given sentence.
  • The above sentence is an example of a use of objective personal pronouns after prepositions or verb.
  • An object pronoun is a type of personal pronoun that is normally used as a grammatical object, either as the direct or indirect object of a verb, or as the object of a preposition.
  • The most common objective personal pronouns are:
    • "Me, you, us, him, her, and them"
  • As per the general rule, a pronoun should be used in the objective case in a sentence beginning with 'Let'.
  • Example:
    • Let her submit the records in time. (correct)
    • Let she submit the records in time. (incorrect)
  • According to the explanation given above, ‘me’ is the correct use in place of “I”.

Correct sentence: Let me do this work for my bright future.

question:
Direction: Fill in the blank with suitable tense forms of the verb.

I ______ for my pen. Have you seen it?
solution:
The correct answer is- 'Am looking.'

Key Points

  • We can see that the second part of the question is in the Present Perfect Tense.
  • The present perfect is often used for an action that started at some time in the past and is still continuing now. The action of "seeing the pen" has been completed in the past and the search for the pen is still going on.
  • Therefore, the first part of the question must be in the Present Continous Tense.
  • The present continuous tense is used to describe dynamic actions that happen repeatedly, are currently happening, or will be happening in the near future.
  • Structure: Subject + is/am/are + V1+ing + Object
  • So, the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct sentence: I am looking for my pen. Have you seen it?

question:
Which of the options given below is the correct passive form of the given sentence?

They crowned him king.
options: He was crowned king by us.
solution:
The correct answer is- He was crowned king.

Additional Information

  • The given sentence is in an active voice form, hence we need to convert it into a passive voice form.
  • Find the subject (They) and object (him) of the sentence and exchange their places. 
  • The given sentence is in the simple past tense. The passive verb form for simple past is: 
    • was/were + past participle form of the verb.
    • So, 'crowned' changes to 'was crowned'.
  • At last line up the remaining part.

  • Following these steps, we finally get- He was crowned king.

Additional Information  ​​​​

  • If the subject isn't clear, the agent (by + Sub.) needn't be mentioned in the passive voice.
  • Example:
    • People follow this ritual all over the world. (active)
    • This ritual is followed all over the world. (passive)

question:
Which one of the following parts of the sentence has an error?

Don't ask him how he is because if he starts talking about his health you'll never get off from him.
options: Don't ask him how he is because
if he starts talking about his health you'll never
solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., get off from him.

Key Points

  •  Option 3 uses the incorrect verb 'get off' from him.
  •  The phrasal verb Get off means leave work at the end of the day. Example: I usually get off at four in the evening.
  •  Given the context, the speaker means to say 'to move or getaway' from 'him'.
  •  So, the correct phrasal verb here would be 'Getaway'.


Thus, the rectified sentence is: Don't ask him how he is because if he starts talking about his health you'll never get away from him.

question:
Direction: Fill in the blank with correct word:

You should practice so that you do not _______ the match.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Lose.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is a negative sentence and in the Present Tense.
  • The present simple, in its negative form, has this structure: Subject + do/does + not + verb + object
    • Example: He does not go there.
  • ​So, we need a base form of the verb in the blank,
  • Let us see the part of speech of the given options:
    • Loose: Adjective, Verb
    • Lose: Verb
    • Losing: Verb
    • Lost: Adjective
  • ​Out of all the options, the base form of verbs are "Lose" and "Loose."
  • "Loose" means set free; release; to speak or express emotions very freely, especially in an uncontrolled way, and "Lose" means to fail to succeed in a game, competition, etc.
  • Now, we are talking about practising to win the match.
  • So, the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct sentence: You should practice so that you do not lose the match.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The guard told the children to stay away from the flower beds.
options: The guard said, “Children, should you stay away from the flower beds.”
The guard said, “Children, stay away from the flower beds.”
The guard told to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”
The guard says to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”
solution:
The correct answer is "The guard said, “Children, stay away from the flower beds.”

Key Points

  • There are a few things to keep in mind when changing a sentence from indirect to direct speech.
  • In the given sentence, the reporting verb "told" changes to "said" in direct speech as this is a first-person narrative.
  • As the guard is saying the sentence to the children., there should be a comma after children to put emphasis on them within the inverted commas.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
